scope: isolated local actual-byte transfer and persistent-profile Chrome restart

code.changed: Only reset transfer backoff after confirmed forward progress, not unchanged successful probes.

regression.before: A repeated 503 followed by an unchanged 308 probe reset failure count and retried indefinitely at the shortest delay.
regression.after: Bounded increasing backoff survives unchanged probes; only real progress resets it.

procedure: Generate and fully write non-sparse 1/3/5 GiB sources to disk; calculate SHA-256 while generating.
Use the actual Upload files action and native File objects from paths. Retain input identity across rerenders; no source payload is constructed in browser memory.
The direct-upload URL is supplied by an isolated provider. An XHR destination adapter routes bytes to a loopback HTTP receiver. Google credentials and network are not used.
Interrupt with a local provider gate at 128 MiB, 1 GiB + 8 MiB, and 4 GiB + 8 MiB respectively. Confirm the encrypted IndexedDB journal before closing.
Close the entire isolated Chrome browser, wait for its OS process to exit, and open a new process with the same persistent profile.
No storage-state export/import, cookie injection, checkpoint injection or sessionStorage restoration is used. Fresh tab session fallback is empty.
The fixture disables File System Access selection, exercising original-file reselection, also used in browsers without persistent source handles.
Resume from the same provider session after source identity verification. Confirm exact chunk offsets, a single catalog record and complete destination bytes.
The 5 GiB queue includes a paused 32 MiB companion. Both entries survive restart; the companion does not advance while only the large original is selected, then resumes after its own selection.
Stream-read completed destination files for independent SHA-256 comparison, then remove only owned verified source/destination fixtures.
limitations: Google Drive/Aeza transfers, Google OAuth, real internet throughput, OS crashes/power loss and physical phones are not covered.
The byte payloads are synthetic MP4-named files; video decoding/playback is not tested.
Chrome on Windows with a persistent ordinary profile is tested. Mobile checks are viewport layouts, not physical iOS/Android acceptance.
Automatic reuse of native OS file handles after a browser restart is not established by this fallback-path run.
Durable checkpoints were allowed to settle before browser close. Abrupt termination before the first checkpoint and clearing the browser profile are not certified.
Timings include hashing, loopback transfer, scripted interruption and catalog registration. They are not production throughput benchmarks.
HTTP 503 gates intentionally retry unconfirmed data. The no-retransmission result concerns confirmed chunks, not all attempted wire bytes.
